gaps.concept: Zona glomerulosa aldosterone secretion responds chiefly to angiotensin II and elevated potassium, with little sustained dependence on ACTH.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies the adrenal layer and stimulus when a stem changes potassium, renin, or ACTH.

gaps.concept: Aldosterone increases ENaC and Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase activity in principal cells and hydrogen secretion by intercalated cells.
gaps.why_tested: Explains sodium retention, potassium loss, and metabolic alkalosis in a mechanism question.

gaps.concept: Familial hyperaldosteronism type I results from a CYP11B1–CYP11B2 fusion that makes aldosterone ACTH-responsive and glucocorticoid-suppressible.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies inherited, early-onset hypertension that improves with glucocorticoid suppression.

gaps.concept: 17α-hydroxylase deficiency increases deoxycorticosterone, causing hypertension and hypokalemia with low renin, low aldosterone, and impaired sexual development.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes this enzyme deficiency from other causes of mineralocorticoid excess.

gaps.concept: 11β-HSD2 normally converts cortisol to cortisone; its loss lets cortisol activate mineralocorticoid receptors despite low aldosterone.
gaps.why_tested: Explains the hormone pattern after licorice ingestion or inherited apparent mineralocorticoid excess.

gaps.concept: Spironolactone can cause gynecomastia through antiandrogen effects; eplerenone is more selective for mineralocorticoid receptors.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes adverse effects of the two drugs used for bilateral adrenal hyperplasia.

gaps.concept: Adrenal medullary chromaffin cells derive from neural crest and act as modified sympathetic postganglionic neurons stimulated by preganglionic acetylcholine.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies embryologic origin or the receptor mediating stress-induced catecholamine release.

gaps.concept: Cortisol from the adrenal cortex induces medullary PNMT, promoting conversion of norepinephrine to epinephrine.
gaps.why_tested: Explains why the adrenal medulla produces epinephrine and why extra-adrenal tumors may produce less.

gaps.concept: Tyrosine hydroxylase catalyzes the rate-limiting step of catecholamine synthesis and is inhibited by metyrosine.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies the enzyme or drug target in a catecholamine synthesis question.

gaps.concept: COMT converts epinephrine and norepinephrine to metanephrine and normetanephrine, respectively.
gaps.why_tested: Connects the measured metabolites to the catecholamines produced by a suspected pheochromocytoma.

gaps.concept: Extra-adrenal sympathetic chromaffin tumors are paragangliomas; head and neck parasympathetic paragangliomas are usually nonsecretory.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes an adrenal catecholamine-secreting mass from a similar extra-adrenal or nonsecretory tumor.

gaps.concept: Tumor manipulation, anesthesia, and surgery can precipitate a pheochromocytoma hypertensive crisis.
gaps.why_tested: Explains abrupt severe hypertension during a procedure on an unsuspected adrenal mass.

gaps.concept: MEN2A pairs pheochromocytoma with medullary thyroid carcinoma and hyperparathyroidism; MEN2B features medullary thyroid carcinoma, mucosal neuromas, and marfanoid habitus.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes the RET-associated syndromes from accompanying findings in a pheochromocytoma stem.

gaps.concept: SDHB-associated paragangliomas have a higher metastatic risk than many other hereditary pheochromocytoma or paraganglioma syndromes.
gaps.why_tested: Links a specific SDH mutation to an aggressive extra-adrenal tumor.

gaps.concept: Metastasis to tissue without normal chromaffin cells establishes metastatic pheochromocytoma; zellballen histology alone cannot establish that behavior.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes a characteristic microscopic pattern from evidence of metastatic disease.

gaps.concept: Catecholamine excess in pheochromocytoma can cause hyperglycemia through reduced insulin secretion and increased hepatic glucose output.
gaps.why_tested: Explains hyperglycemia accompanying episodic hypertension and adrenergic symptoms.

gaps.concept: Neuroblastoma metastases can cause periorbital ecchymoses and proptosis or bluish skin nodules in infants.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies an adrenal medullary tumor from characteristic metastatic findings in a young child.

gaps.concept: Some neuroblastomas secrete vasoactive intestinal peptide, producing profuse watery diarrhea and hypokalemia.
gaps.why_tested: Connects otherwise unexplained secretory diarrhea with a pediatric sympathetic tumor.

gaps.concept: Neuroblastoma can show tumor calcifications and encasement of major vessels on abdominal imaging.
gaps.why_tested: Helps distinguish a pediatric adrenal mass from a renal mass on imaging.

gaps.concept: Germline activating ALK mutations predispose to familial neuroblastoma.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies the inherited mutation in a child with neuroblastoma and affected relatives.
